# Fixed: Fingerprint every release, and stop rejecting a file when AcoustID names a sibling recording of the same song

Part of the [custom Lidarr image](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/tree/custom) (`ghcr.io/chodeus/lidarr:custom`), which merges this branch into `develop`. It is stacked on `feat/metadata-source-ids`, which only compares MusicBrainz ids, and merges after it. Reviewed in [#PR_NUMBER](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/pull/PR_NUMBER).

For a fingerprinted file, `DistanceCalculator.TrackDistance` adds the `recording_id` penalty unless AcoustID names the track's own MusicBrainz recording. Its weight of 10 is the heaviest in a track's distance. MusicBrainz often holds one song as several recordings, one per release, and AcoustID can file the fingerprint under a sibling from another release. A right file without a MusicBrainz recording tag then scores 37.5% against the 60% a new download needs, and the whole album is rejected as "Worst track match".

- The lookup sent every fingerprint of a release in one request. AcoustID took 20 ordinary fingerprints (70 KB) in one request but answered 30 (104 KB) with error 19, "request too large", which was logged only at Debug, so a bigger release got no AcoustID results and no recording check at all. Fingerprints now go at most 10 to a request, and a request that times out after 5 seconds is tried once more. A request that still fails leaves its own files without results, as before; if AcoustID didn't answer it at all, the rest aren't sent, so a hung service costs one timeout and its retry, not one per batch.
- The AcoustID lookup asks for `meta=recordings` instead of `meta=recordingids`, which adds each named recording's title, length and artists. `LocalTrack.AcoustIdResults` holds the same ids as before; the rest goes in a new `LocalTrack.AcoustIdRecordings`. On 89 fingerprints, both requests named the same recordings above the score threshold.
- A named recording with the track's title, by the track's artist and within 3 seconds of the track's length costs 0.2 instead of the full penalty. Titles are compared as letters and digits only, ignoring case and accents on Latin letters; marks in other scripts, such as Japanese voicing marks or Hindi and Tamil vowel signs, change the word and count. A file for which it is the only miss scores 87.5% instead of 37.5%, and an album made only of such files stays under the album threshold. A named recording without a title, a length or artists, a track without a length, and a lookup without titles, such as an identification test case, are penalised as before.
- The track's own recording still costs nothing. So a release holding the recording AcoustID named ranks above one holding a sibling, and two same-titled tracks on one release keep their own files. On a single the gap is one track's worth, so a tag field such as country or label that favours the sibling's release can still decide which edition wins.
- A recording with another title, or by another artist, still counts against the file, so a cut titled "(instrumental)" that AcoustID files under the vocal recording, a remix filed under the original, or another act's song of the same name keeps the penalty. MusicBrainz often gives a live, clean or remastered version the original's title, so such a version within 3 seconds of the track's length is charged 0.2 too. Live cuts rarely come that close; same-length clean or explicit versions do.

Tests: in `TrackDistanceFixture`, a named recording with the track's title, also punctuated differently, also with a Latin accent, and a length up to 3 seconds either side costs 0.2, as does one credited to the track's artist among others, and the track's own recording costs nothing; another title, an instrumental label, an empty title, a length 3.5 seconds off either way or 10 seconds off, no length (also against a 2-second track), another artist, no artists, a track without a length, no titles at all, two empty titles a Japanese, Thai, Hindi or Tamil title differing only by a mark, and one differing only by a character beyond the Basic Multilingual Plane, cost the full penalty, while a title made only of such characters matches itself. `SiblingRecordingFixture` goes through the real `MapReleaseTracks` and `AlbumReleaseDistance`: two same-titled tracks map to their own recordings, the release holding the named recording ranks first, also for a five-track album against a sibling release in a preferred country, a file named under a sibling stays within the track threshold, and a fifteen-track album of them within the album threshold. In `FingerprintingServiceFixture`, 23 fingerprints go out as requests of 10, 10 and 3 and each file gets its own answer; a batch that times out twice keeps the earlier batches' results and stops the rest, so a hung service gets 2 requests for 30 fingerprints; a timed-out request is tried once more and its answer used, and another kind of failure isn't retried. The request asks for `meta=recordings`, and the response's titles, lengths and artists are kept beside the ids through the real JSON parsing, a recording without them is kept with none, and a result below the score threshold is left out. The recorded AcoustID requests in `AcoustidResponses.json` now say `meta=recordings`; their responses stay as recorded, with ids only, so the titles, lengths and artists come only from the inline response. Twenty-nine mutations each fail a test: requests of 30, no retry, retrying any failure, retrying three times or without limit, sending the rest after an unanswered request, never marking one unanswered, dropping characters beyond the Basic Multilingual Plane, keeping the full penalty for a sibling, waiving it, a sibling penalty of 0.05 or 0.5, charging the track's own recording, ignoring the title, the length or the artist, accepting a recording without artists, a 4-second, 10-second or strict 3-second tolerance, no check on the track's length or on a missing recording length, stripping every mark or none, dropping spacing marks, matching two empty titles, asking for `meta=recordingids`, not keeping the recordings, and keeping recordings below the score threshold.
